testResults.name: integration-wiring
testResults.result: Coordinator wired facades: venues/__init__ (Alpaca broker + crypto venue surfaces), risk/__init__ (collateral + kill switch), runtime/__init__ (state store), testing/__init__ (paper parity), results/__init__ (offline HTML report), data/__init__ (OPRA + options replay); repository.md rows updated for harness.http, harness.venues, harness.risk, harness.testing, harness.results, harness.runtime, thesis.workflows, and the thesis process boundary/image.

integrationHistory: Eleven-lane fan-out with exclusive file ownership across H6/H7, harness H3/H4, and Thesis TH1/TH6.

Key findings carried to follow-ups: options multi-leg is not yet runnable through the backtest runner (T120 hand-composed the kernel in tests; runner options-venue wiring is the gap), MarketLakeAdapter rejects asset_class=OPTION (options replay needs a lakeclient-backed partition port), risk pipeline _BUILTINS lacks aliases for the new rules, PaperShell capability surfaces trail the backtest engine (plain EventScheduler/HistoricalView vs StrategyScheduler/StrategyHistory), Dockerfile.thesis needs CI publication wiring, remote backtest polling loop deferred, and MultiLegOrder cannot express net-credit/debit without a venue-adapter mapping convention.
limitations: Live broker venues are untested against the real Alpaca API (deterministic fakes only, per repo policy); first live-paper contact is a gated operations task under H7.
Kill switch ships the explicit in-runtime switch; Azure-flag polling and authenticated CLI controls per the T110 spec are separate cloud/CLI work.
StateStore restore is state-identical but not event-identical for subsequent strategy callbacks until PaperShell exposes binding capture (documented in T108 findings).
